maria: Repro note: sampleapp background sync (WorkManager) + Retrofit + OkHttp. We see OkHttp calls "canceled" during backoff when device locks on Android 14. Logs:

I/OkHttp: --> POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/feature
W/OkHttp: callTimedOut: canceling
I/OkHttp: <-- HTTP FAILED: java.io.IOException: canceled
E/App: Auth refresh start
I/OkHttp: --> POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/feature
I/OkHttp: <-- 401 Unauthorized
E/App: Auth refresh done
I/OkHttp: <-- HTTP FAILED: java.io.IOException: canceled

maria: Retry implementation: we used a coroutine-friendly CallAdapter in prod, but quick repro used an Interceptor with runBlocking for delays. Suspect cancellation from worker scope cascades to Call and cancels next attempt.

alex: runBlocking in interceptor is a red flag. If the outer coroutine is cancelled, Call.cancel() will be invoked by Retrofit. Use suspendCancellableCoroutine wrapper around Call.enqueue and invokeOnCancellation to cancel.

ben: Also check HTTP/2 multiplexing. If you cancel and recreate calls while changing Authorization header, connection coalescing can cause surprising cancellations. Try client.protocols = listOf(Protocol.HTTP_1_1) as a quick experiment.

ciara: WorkManager may stop workers aggressively when device is idle. If backoff delays live on the worker's coroutine scope, OS stops -> scope.cancel -> okhttp call cancelled. Try moving delays to a separate supervisorScope that isn't cancelled by WorkManager, or persist retry state and reschedule the Worker.

maria: Good tips. I'll: 1) flip to suspend wrapper for Calls; 2) test disabling HTTP/2; 3) add EventListener logs to capture callStart/callFailed order; 4) push small reproducible branch and link PR.

nate: For quick repro, adb shell svc wifi disable while waiting in backoff. Also try toggling Dispatchers.IO vs Default for the backoff to see if thread starvation matters.
